title: 3.4 questions and comments
body:
### Ask or discuss any quick questions about 3.4 here please.

**Do not use this issue for bug reports,** please open a new issue with full information, see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**[The 3.4 CHANGES file is here](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.4/CHANGES).**

As always, thanks to the many people who contributed to both this and to previous releases.

That comment in the change log is from 2009, and refers to tmux 0.6 😁

I think there's a small bug that's been introduced into the cmd-split-window.c on line 98:

` size = args_strtonum_and_expand(args, 'l', 0, 100, item,`

Which I think should be:

` size = args_strtonum_and_expand(args, 'p', 0, 100, item,`

I rebuilt a local copy of tmux with that alteration and that seems to have fixed the issue for me.

I've also raised a PR with this small fix in it.

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
The oh-my-zsh plugin has an alias "ta" which maps to `tmux attach-session -t`. Tmux version 3.3a allowed passing `-t` without any arguments, but no longer does in 3.4. In order to make a fix that works for users of 3.3a and 3.4, I would propose just calling `tmux attach-session` without any flags. `tmux attach-session` and `tmux attach-session -t` seem to do identical things and works with both versions. Could anyone here confirm if that is correct?

Edit: Amending this to say that my assumption was not correct. Aliasing `tmux attach-session -t` is better since it allows you to pass a session name. So, `ta SESSION` would no longer work if we can't pass an empty flag. New question then: is there a good way to just run the alias without needing to pass a session name as before?

comments.author: participant17
comments.body:
> Edit: Amending this to say that my assumption was not correct. Aliasing `tmux attach-session -t` is better since it allows you to pass a session name. So, `ta SESSION` would no longer work if we can't pass an empty flag. New question then: is there a good way to just run the alias without needing to pass a session name as before?

I don't think it's doable with a simple alias. It needs to be turned into a function, like so:

```zsh
function ta() {
    tmux attach-session ${1:+-t }$1
}
```

Thanks for digging deeper and refining your initial report, @participant27. I'm still not able to reproduce and the commands given in the example could use an existing session or otherwise be affected by the environment.

Here's my take on the example commands to ensure no existing session is used and no empty `.tmux.conf` is needed:

```sh
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
tmux -vv -f/dev/null new
tmux -vv -f/dev/null split-window -h -l 90% # run from shell created within the tmux session
tmux display-message -p '#{client_width}x#{client_height}: #{window_layout}'
80x24: 0e73,80x23,0,0{7x23,0,0,0,72x23,8,0,1}
```

```sh
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
tmux -vv -f/dev/null new -d \
&& tmux -vv -f/dev/null split-window -h -l 90% \
&& tmux -f/dev/null attach
tmux display-message -p '#{client_width}x#{client_height}: #{window_layout}' # run from shell created within the tmux session
80x24: 0e73,80x23,0,0{7x23,0,0,0,72x23,8,0,1}
```

comments.author: participant29
comments.body:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/3836#issuecomment-2091678394

Just found this in the changelog:

> * Change so that {} is converted to tmux commands immediately when parsed. This
  means it must contain valid tmux commands. For commands which expand %% and
  %%%, this now only happens within string arguments. Use of nested aliases
  inside {} is now forbidden. Processing of commands given in quotes remains
  the same.

Umm what? Why?? It was a generalized "", used to encode arbitrary strings to be sent to and interpreted by arbitrary commands such as "run", which interprets it as a shell command obviously. It's still documented as such in the 3.4 manpage. 

And now all of a sudden it can only be used for tmux commands? What sense does that make??

Issue with Panel Splitting in tmux 3.4

Description
In tmux version 3.4, I encountered an issue where the first script evenly splits the window into 8 panels, but the second script does not. However, both scripts work correctly in tmux version 2.3, evenly splitting the window into 8 panels.

Script 1
This script splits the window evenly into 8 panels in both tmux 2.3 and 3.4:
```
tmux new -s ttt -d
tmux splitw -v -l 50% -t ttt:0.0
tmux splitw -h -l 75% -t ttt:0.0
tmux splitw -h -l 66% -t ttt:0.1
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.2
tmux splitw -h -l 75% -t ttt:0.4
tmux splitw -h -l 66% -t ttt:0.5
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.6
tmux attach -t ttt
```

Script 2
This script splits the window evenly into 8 panels in tmux 2.3, but not in tmux 3.4:
```
tmux new -s ttt -d
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.0
tmux splitw -v -l 50% -t ttt:0.1
tmux splitw -v -l 50% -t ttt:0.0
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.3
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.2
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.1
tmux splitw -h -l 50% -t ttt:0.0
tmux attach -t ttt
```
Steps to Reproduce
Run the scripts in tmux 3.4 and tmux 2.3 respectively.
Observe the panel distribution and verify if they are split evenly into 8 panels.

Expected Behavior
Both scripts should split the window evenly into 8 panels in tmux 3.4, just as they do in tmux 2.3.

Actual Behavior
In tmux 3.4, Script 1 splits the window evenly into 8 panels, but Script 2 does not.

Environment
tmux version: 3.4 (issue present)
tmux version: 2.3 (no issue)

Please investigate this inconsistency between tmux versions.

Thank you!

I noticed that when starting a new tmux window/pane, the following message is generated in the system logs:

```systemd[3083]: Started tmux-spawn-3fb77461-07bc-49d7-888b-574c631b7b07.scope - tmux child pane 266522 launched by process 3390.```

Is there a way to forbid creating `tmux-spawn-*.scope`? The reason is a problem with cgroupsv2. After reloading the configuration, everything works well for some time, till it happens again.
